clue.text: Out in the open, before the line is official

parts.note: to come forth is to come out into the open
ere is an old word for before
a cord is a line or length of string

explanation.surface: Someone making a statement in public, insisting it becomes official once a line has been drawn.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like the phrase itself explained, but it is a charade: FORTH, then ERE, then CORD, with 'is' as the link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something said so it is noted and on public file is said officially, as part of the formal account.

clue.text: 24, for instance, are sick of coming up

indicators.note: coming up in a down clue means the pieces read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: eg is the abbreviation meaning for instance
to ail is to be ill

explanation.surface: Examples of people who become ill when something comes up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming up' turns EG AIL OF, giving FO LIA GE. '24' is the answer to 24 across, LEAFAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Leafage and this word are both collective terms for a plant's leaves.

clue.text: Heard from Alexander, possibly — "I'm great!

indicators.note: possibly says the following letters may be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A boast heard from someone called Alexander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges I'M GREAT. The definition alludes to Irving Berlin's song Alexander's Ragtime Band.
explanation.definitionFit: Irving Berlin's 1911 hit is about Alexander's band, which plays syncopated piano-style music of that era.

clue.text: In the gloaming, Henry goes on a journey

indicators.note: goes on means the journey follows straight after the name

parts.note: Hal is a pet name for Henry, as for Shakespeare's Prince Hal
a flight is a journey by air

explanation.surface: At dusk, Henry sets out on a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes on' joins HAL and FLIGHT; 'In the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The gloaming is twilight, when dim light fades at dusk.

clue.text: Fend off pawn in' lively movement

indicators.note: in means the chess piece is placed inside the dance

parts.note: a reel is a lively Scottish dance
P is the chess abbreviation for pawn

explanation.surface: Fighting off a pawn's spirited advance on the chessboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts P inside REEL, a lively Scottish dance.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive back an attacker is to ward them off.

clue.text: Force one into club in the South West

indicators.note: into means the force and one are put inside the club

parts.note: a cosh is a short heavy club
RN, the Royal Navy, is an armed force
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A tale of forcing someone into a nightclub in the West Country.
explanation.walkthrough: The held text reads 'late', an OCR misread of 'into' on the printed page. RN, the Royal Navy, is the force.
explanation.definitionFit: Cornwall is the county at the tip of England's South West, and this adjective means from there.

clue.text: Find a new place for the lady upriver

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word for the lady is read from the bottom

parts.note: her refers to a lady
the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: Moving a woman to a house further up the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upriver' splits in two: 'up' is the reversal signal for a down clue, and 'river' is the Ouse, a river in Yorkshire and elsewhere in England.
explanation.definitionFit: To relocate someone to fresh housing is to give them a new home.

clue.text: Some steps relieving air conditioning

indicators.note: conditioning changes the state of something, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Air conditioning bringing relief to people on the stairs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conditioning' rearranges RELIEVING AIR, twelve letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An American country dance is made up of a sequence of dance steps.

clue.text: It's unhealthy holding on to a criminal

indicators.note: holding means the first piece keeps the following words inside it

parts.note: unhealthy means ill
in cricket the on side is also called the leg side, so on gives LEG

explanation.surface: A sick person clinging to a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' as LEG is a cricket convention: the leg side is the on side. 'It's' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A criminal act is one that breaks the law, so as an adjective the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Page bowed, then dried up

parts.note: something bowed is curved, arched

explanation.surface: A young servant bows, then wilts in the heat.
explanation.definitionFit: Parched land has been dried out by heat and lack of water.

clue.text: Saxon artefacts found in town and country

parts.note: Dresden is a city in Saxony
China is a country

explanation.surface: Saxon relics turn up in towns and countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine porcelain from Meissen near Dresden in Saxony is known by this name.

clue.text: A Gallic recipe for the making of ice

indicators.note: a recipe tells how to make something from ingredients, so the letters that follow are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A French way of making ice, perhaps sorbet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recipe for the making' rearranges the seven letters of A GALLIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Glacial describes glaciers and ice, meaning icy or frozen.

clue.text: Flowers of course are free at this

parts.note: a lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers
sure, as a reply, means of course

explanation.surface: Flowers, naturally, are free to enjoy at this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flowers' suggests rivers or blooms in general; here it is the garland LEI. 'are' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone at their own pace with spare time is said to be free, having time off work.

clue.text: Relative starts to notice ignorance each child exhibits

indicators.note: starts to these words means their opening letters are taken in turn

explanation.surface: A family member notices how ignorant every child is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starts to' takes the first letter of each of the five words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a family member, a relation by blood.

clue.text: Sticks one had around for protection during fight

parts.note: to gum is to stick, so sticks gives GUMS

indicators.note: around means the word for had is placed about the letter for one

parts.note: had in the sense of possessed is held
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone holding sticks to protect themselves in a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sticks' looks like a noun for rods but is the verb, glues. A gumshield is a boxer's mouthguard.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxer wears a mouthguard to protect the teeth in a bout.

clue.text: Girl embraces being unmarried and 23

indicators.note: embraces means the girl's name goes round the other piece

parts.note: Maria is a girl's name

indicators.note: M is the abbreviation for married, so unmarried takes that letter away

parts.note: a being is a human

explanation.surface: A girl embracing single life and something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unmarried' leaves HUAN, since M stands for married in registers and family trees; 23 is the answer at 23 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Hashish is resin from cannabis, as this is the dried plant, both drugs from hemp.

clue.text: Put in different form, two scholars entering old school

indicators.note: entering means the scholars go inside the word for changing form

parts.note: to alter is to put something in a different form
MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar's degree; two of them give two copies
the second of the two MA scholars

explanation.surface: Changing an old school by bringing in a pair of academics.
explanation.walkthrough: MA is Master of Arts, so 'two scholars' gives the pair of letters twice.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase, literally nourishing mother, names the college or school a person attended.

clue.text: Travelling players in the wrong parts?

definitions.text: Travelling players in the wrong parts?

parts.words: Travelling players in the wrong parts?
parts.note: touring actors given roles that do not suit them have been badly chosen for those roles

explanation.surface: A touring company whose actors are all playing unsuitable roles.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor given an unsuitable role has been chosen wrongly for it.

clue.text: Material from an unnamed source

indicators.note: from means the answer's letters come out of the word that follows, rearranged

explanation.surface: Information obtained from an anonymous source.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' rearranges UNNAMED; 'an' and 'source' complete the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Material in the sense of worldly or earthly, as opposed to spiritual, is everyday.

clue.text: What a sap, to go wrong again!

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
to sin is to go wrong morally

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a fool who has gone astray a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sap' looks like a fool, but it is the plant fluid; RE comes first even though 'again' ends the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Resin is the sticky substance exuded from trees like pines, a kind of plant secretion.

clue.text: The rest have to live without you, so to speak

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside means the word for live goes around the next piece

parts.note: to reside is to live somewhere

indicators.note: so to speak means the word you is taken by its sound alone

parts.note: the letter U is said like the word you

explanation.surface: Those left behind have to manage without you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside, so RESIDE goes around U, said like 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is what remains, the remainder left over.

clue.text: In prison, Communist is moved

parts.note: stir is slang for prison, so to be in stir is to be in jail
red is a common term for a communist

explanation.surface: A jailed Communist is emotionally affected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To be stirred is to be emotionally touched or affected.

clue.text: Delicatessen certainly stocks this concentrate

indicators.note: a shop stocks goods, so the word is held within these letters

explanation.surface: A delicatessen is bound to sell this flavouring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stocks' points to letters held inside DELICATESSEN CERTAINLY.
explanation.definitionFit: An extract made by boiling down or distilling, such as vanilla extract, is a concentrate.

clue.text: Raise before and heartlessly cut after

indicators.note: after means the shortened word comes after the first piece

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

indicators.note: heartlessly means the middle letter of the word cut is removed

explanation.surface: Lift it first, and then trim it without feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' leaves CT, which comes 'after' ERE; the heart of a three-letter word is its middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To erect something is to set it upright, to build or put up.

clue.text: The man's in a stew-pot

indicators.note: in means the man's possessive goes inside the word for a stew

parts.note: hash is a stew of chopped meat
his means belonging to the man

explanation.surface: A man seated in a cooking pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stew-pot' looks like one object, but the hyphen splits wordplay from the definition, pot.
explanation.definitionFit: Pot is slang for cannabis, and cannabis resin is called this.

clue.text: Leaves a cigarette in the shelter

indicators.note: in means a cigarette goes inside the word for shelter

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
fag is British slang for a cigarette

explanation.surface: Someone who slips out for a smoke in a shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: FAG is everyday British slang for a cigarette, not an insult here.
explanation.definitionFit: The collected leaves of a plant form its greenery or foliage.

clue.text: Dog with mettle, we hear

parts.note: with means and, as in bread with butter
mettle said aloud is metal, and iron is a metal

explanation.surface: A spirited dog, by all accounts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mettle, we hear' is heard as 'metal', of which iron is an example; a firedog is a support for logs in a fireplace.
explanation.definitionFit: A firedog is a metal support for logs in a hearth, also called this.

clue.text: Scattering seeds that are vastly superior

indicators.note: scattering seeds disperses them, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener sowing seeds that are far better than the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scattering' rearranges SEEDS THAT ARE, twelve letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means far ahead of rivals, much better.
